title: Load orders and handle request failures
outcome: Return a useful result when order loading succeeds, fails, or returns the wrong shape.
story: The inbox needs to load orders from a service. The network can be slow, a response can be an error, and a successful status can still contain unexpected data.

frames.explanation: The interface waits for the response before using the result.

values.label: screen
values.value: Could not load orders. Try again.

frames.explanation: A failure should replace the loading state with a useful next action.

sections.title: Programs can ask another program
paragraphs: An HTTP request asks a server to do something. A GET request commonly reads information. The server returns a status, headers, and a body. JSON is one common format for the body.

A URL identifies the destination. An endpoint is a particular operation exposed by the service, such as GET /orders. Agree on the response shape: our practice order list contains objects with an id and a totalCents value.

sections.title: A request finishes later
paragraphs: An asynchronous operation returns a promise for a future result. async marks a function that can wait for promises. await waits for an operation inside that function without pretending its result is already available.

A page can show Loading while a request is in progress. After it finishes, show the data, an empty state, or an error. Keep these states distinct so an empty order list is not mistaken for a broken service.

sections.title: Check status and data shape
paragraphs: fetch does not automatically reject every HTTP error status. Check response.ok before reading the body. Then await response.json() and validate the data shape before handing it to the interface.

A response with status 200 and a JSON object is still wrong if the contract requires an array. A row with a negative total or missing identifier also breaks the contract. Use the validation habits you already practised with saved baskets.

sections.title: Recover without hiding the problem
paragraphs: Network failures and JSON parsing errors can throw. Catch them and return a useful error result. Avoid an infinite retry loop: give the person a deliberate Try again action and make operations safe to repeat.

The exercise injects a prepared request function to test these outcomes reliably. It does not call a live service. The project connects the same adapter to real fetch and checks browser network behaviour against your local backend.

exercise.title: A reliable order adapter
exercise.brief: Implement loadOrders(request). Return { ok: true, orders } for valid data, or { ok: false, error } using http, shape, or network. The exercise supplies a prepared request function.
exercise.starter: async function loadOrders(request) { return { ok: true, orders: [] }; }

steps.title: Wait for valid orders
steps.task: Call and await request(), then await response.json(). Return the orders in a success result.
steps.hint: Keep the supplied request fixture. Write an async loadOrders function with two awaits.

steps.title: Handle HTTP and network failures
steps.task: Preserve the complete supplied request fixture. Return http for !response.ok and network for thrown request or JSON errors.
steps.hint: Put the request and body reading inside try/catch. An HTTP error should be handled before reading the body.

steps.title: Validate returned records
steps.task: Require an array. Every record needs an integer id and a non-negative integer totalCents. Return shape otherwise.
steps.hint: Validate the array and every row after reading JSON. An empty array is valid.

cases.label: A valid response
cases.why: The adapter must preserve intended success.

cases.label: An empty order list
cases.why: No orders is a valid result.

cases.label: An HTTP failure
cases.why: A failed status must not become a successful empty list.

cases.label: A failed connection
cases.why: A thrown request needs a deliberate error result.

cases.label: Unreadable response JSON
cases.why: An unreadable body cannot be used as order data.

cases.label: The wrong JSON shape
cases.why: A successful status does not prove the response contract.

cases.label: A negative order total
cases.why: Validate records inside the list as well as the list itself.

project.title: A reliable order-loading screen
project.brief: Build a loading adapter and a view with loading, empty, success, and error states. Begin with prepared requests; connect it to your real service in lesson 17.
deliverables: The adapter and its result contract.
A view for each request state.
A network inspection record after real integration.
